input.summary: The paper claim asserts that adding 20 ms delay under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions changes TCP flow completion time. The user requests a small emulated pilot using the built-in netem runner comparing 0 ms vs. 20 ms additional one-way delay. This proposal designs a bounded emulated-netem-v1 pilot with two client configurations (0 ms and 20 ms delay), a shared bottleneck, and replicated runs to observe the directional effect on flow completion time. No causal or generalizable conclusions can be drawn from a pilot; this is a feasibility and directional check only.
questions: What bottleneck rate (Mbit/s) and buffer size (kbytes) should be used — or should defaults (e.g., 10 Mbit/s, 128 kbytes) be applied for the pilot?
What file transfer size(s) in MBytes should each client use — a single small size (e.g., 1 MByte) or multiple sizes to probe sensitivity?
Should the CCA be fixed to a single algorithm (e.g., cubic) for both clients, or should the pilot also vary CCA (e.g., cubic vs. bbr)?

proposal.problem: It is unknown whether and by how much adding 20 ms of emulated one-way delay changes TCP flow completion time under a fixed bottleneck, as no empirical measurements have been recorded for this claim.
proposal.question: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, does adding 20 ms additional one-way delay produce a measurable difference in TCP flow completion time compared to 0 ms additional delay?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two delay conditions tested within the same emulated bottleneck environment: (A) 0 ms additional one-way delay, (B) 20 ms additional one-way delay. Bottleneck rate proposed at 10 Mbit/s, buffer proposed at 128 kbytes. Two clients per run, each transferring a proposed 1 MByte file. CCA proposed as cubic for both clients. 16 replications per condition (32 total planned units).
proposal.related_work: Source citation: 'Synthetic networking paper claim for development evaluation' (sha256: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa). No full text was provided; coverage is recorded metadata only. The netem Linux traffic control tool is the standard mechanism for emulating delay and loss in kernel-level network emulation. TCP flow completion time is a standard metric in transport-layer evaluation.
proposal.alternatives: Alternative explanations for any observed difference include: (1) bottleneck buffer sizing dominating over delay effects at small file sizes; (2) CCA-specific behavior (e.g., slow-start interactions with RTT) rather than a general delay effect; (3) run-to-run variance in the emulated environment masking or inflating the effect. A broader validation would require multiple CCAs, file sizes, and bottleneck rates.
proposal.design: Proposed emulated pilot using emulated-netem-v1 runner. Two configurations: Config-A uses client_delays_ms=[0,0] and Config-B uses client_delays_ms=[20,20]. All other parameters held constant: 2 clients, cubic CCA for both, 1 MByte file size, 10 Mbit/s bottleneck, 128 kbytes buffer, 0% loss, 100 ms snapshot interval. Each configuration is run with 16 replications. The primary comparison is the distribution of flow_completion_time_ms across the 16 replications of Config-A vs. Config-B. This is a pilot (stage: pilot); no inferential intervals are declared without a justified independent sampling design.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: flow_completion_time_ms (milliseconds) per client per replication. Summary statistics: median and range across replications for each condition. Directional criterion: median FCT in Config-B (20 ms delay) should exceed median FCT in Config-A (0 ms delay) to be consistent with the claim.
proposal.controls: Fixed across both configurations: number of clients (2), CCA (cubic), file size (1 MByte), bottleneck rate (10 Mbit/s), bottleneck buffer (128 kbytes), loss percentage (0%), snapshot interval (100 ms), script (netem_nines.py). Replications held equal (16 per condition).
proposal.falsification: The claim is inconsistent with observations if: (1) median FCT in Config-B (20 ms) is equal to or lower than median FCT in Config-A (0 ms) across replications, OR (2) the range of FCT values across replications fully overlaps between conditions with no directional separation. A pilot cannot establish causality or generalization; a null or reversed result would motivate re-examination of bottleneck parameters, file sizes, or CCA choice before broader validation.
proposal.inputs: Source sha256 (paper claim): aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa. Packet sha256: a1b401caab0920ee2f11377b7285ff0ef7269c187cfa7f3df1c1cb576ba8c0da. Context sha256: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb. Runner: emulated-netem-v1. Script: netem_nines.py. Bottleneck rate, buffer size, file size, and CCA are proposed values pending owner confirmation.
proposal.limitations: 1. Emulated environment (netem) does not replicate real-world path diversity, cross-traffic, or hardware queuing. 2. Only one CCA (cubic) and one file size (1 MByte) are tested; results may not generalize. 3. Only 16 replications per condition; variance estimates are imprecise. 4. No full paper text was provided; the claim context is metadata only. 5. Pilot success cannot establish causality or broader generalization. 6. Proposed bottleneck/buffer/file-size values are unconfirmed by the owner.

questions: What bottleneck rate (Mbit/s) and buffer size (kbytes) should be used, or should proposed defaults (10 Mbit/s, 128 kbytes) apply?
What file transfer size(s) in MBytes should each client use?
Should CCA be fixed to cubic for both clients, or should the pilot also vary CCA?
protocol.hypotheses: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.

metrics.name: flow_completion_time_ms
metrics.criterion: Median FCT in 20 ms delay condition exceeds median FCT in 0 ms delay condition across 16 replications

protocol.dates_or_epochs: To be recorded at execution time; no prior exposure.
protocol.seeds: Not applicable; netem emulation is deterministic given fixed parameters, but run-to-run variance is expected from OS scheduling.

sensitivity.rationale: FCT is sensitive to bottleneck rate, buffer size, and file size. Proposed values are unconfirmed; owner should verify before freezing. A sensitivity check varying file size (e.g., 0.5 and 2 MByte) is recommended in a follow-on main experiment.

protocol.replication_unit: One full run of netem_nines.py with both clients completing their transfers
protocol.sample_size_rationale: 16 replications per condition (32 total) is the maximum allowed within the 32 planned_units constraint. This provides a descriptive range for a pilot; it is insufficient for formal inference but adequate to observe directional consistency.
protocol.exclusions: Runs where either client does not complete transfer (FCT = null or error) will be flagged and reported separately; they will not be included in the median calculation.
protocol.missing_data: If fewer than 8 valid replications per condition are obtained, the pilot result is inconclusive and the bottleneck/buffer parameters should be revisited.
protocol.statistics: Descriptive only: median and range of flow_completion_time_ms per condition per client. No inferential intervals declared; independent sampling design is not established for this emulated pilot.
protocol.dependence: Replications within a condition share the same emulated host environment; run-to-run OS scheduling effects may introduce dependence. Treated as descriptive repeated measurements, not independent samples.

resource_limits.cost_basis: Emulated runner; no cloud compute charges known. Cost unknown.

protocol.stopping_rule: Stop after 32 runs (16 per condition) regardless of intermediate results. Do not retry to obtain a desired directional outcome.
protocol.prior_exposure: No prior measurements recorded for this claim.
protocol.coverage_limits: Results apply only to the specific emulated conditions tested (cubic, 1 MByte, 10 Mbit/s, 128 kbytes buffer). No generalization to real networks, other CCAs, or other file sizes is warranted from this pilot.
protocol.data_origin: Emulated network environment (emulated-netem-v1); not real-world traffic.
